Thanks Mateo — we reviewed the short pilot pricing but procurement pushed back on 12-month minimums. Two asks from our finance lead: 1) can we split the commitment into a 6-month pilot bucket + 18-month commercial bucket (same total $ value), and 2) provide a clear approver ladder so we can circulate the PO internally (they need an exec-level signoff pathway). Any guidance on what buyer tiers AWS Marketplace will require for a split private offer?

Also, low priority but they asked for SOC2 evidence and service activation SLA language. I can pull together their procurement contacts if helpful.

—Liam

Hi Liam — thanks for the detail. Short answer: yes, we can structure a split-duration private offer that maps to different activation/approval windows, but there are a few practical considerations to avoid delays on the AWS side. High-level proposal below, attaching a quick spreadsheet with concrete $/bucket examples.

Proposal (summary):
- Pilot bucket: 6 months, limited to X concurrent seats / usage cap; activation through AWS with standard private-offer workflow.
- Commercial bucket: 18 months, kicks in when pilot thresholds are met or on a calendar date; separate SKU line in the PO so AWS can reconcile activation.
- Total commitment can remain equivalent to their target spend, but pricing for the pilot will be discounted to reflect trial risk.

Buyer approval rail mapping (what to include in the PO to speed approvals):
1) "Finance" bucket: line items and cost center information mapped to buyer CFO — required for invoicing.
2) "Procurement" bucket: procurement contact + PO number placeholder — procurement can circulate without exec signoff.
3) "Exec escalation" clause: an explicit signoff pathway if pilot triggers (names/emails + DocuSign link recommended).

On AWS Marketplace constraints: if you want both buckets to be visible as a single private offer, we need to list them as separate SKUs within the same private-offer contract and request activation windows in the private-offer note to AWS marketplace ops. That typically requires a short back-and-forth with AWS legal/ops (1–3 business days if we provide clear evidence).

I attached: PO_term_buckets_v1.xlsx (sample line-item layout). I can coordinate a short call with our Marketplace ops lead to walk CloudSolve's procurement through the activation flow — Naomi and Jordan, can you join if we set a time tomorrow?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick operational notes from Marketplace/ops:
- AWS private offers support multiple SKUs, but if the buyer wants "deferred activation" for the commercial bucket we must include explicit activation triggers in the private-offer note. Example triggers: (A) pilot consumption > 60% of pilot cap, or (B) calendar date 2028-01-01.
- Evidence: for procurement we can include a zipped evidence pack (SOC2 summary, SLA excerpt, IP location statement). Please send any vendor-specific procurement forms we should preload into the DocuSign packet.
- Approver ladder: AWS doesn't enforce buyer internal approvers, but they will need a clear buyer identifier and a valid billing account. So the fastest path is to provide a single PO with 2 SKU lines and a doc (1 page) that lists the internal approver ladder and DocuSign routing instructions.

Sofia — if we provide the evidence pack and the one-page approver ladder, ops can push the private-offer to AWS with a note for conditional activation. I put a short checklist below.

Checklist (for CloudSolve):
- PO with two SKU lines (pilot/commercial) + total contract value.
- Billing account ARN or buyer account email.
- Approver ladder document (names, titles, emails) for DocuSign routing.
- SOC2 summary + any additional compliance evidence.

If CloudSolve can drop the approver ladder and PO by tomorrow EOD, we can target a 48–72 hour turnaround on AWS-side submission.

—Naomi
Marketplace Ops, Redwood Inference

That gives our PMs time to verify production readiness.

I've attached: CS_PO_draft.pdf and CS_approver_chart.xlsx. If you can confirm both items (esp pilot-rate preservation), we'll route to our CFO for the exec signoff lane.
